prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1449; do not mention it.)
text:
I write on behalf of our client, who was injured in a head-on collision and is now represented by this firm in connection with the resulting claim. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. If your insured or any representative of your company has already been in contact with our client, please let us know so that we can address it.

We ask that you provide the policy limits for the liability coverage applicable to the at-fault driver, along with a copy of the declarations page confirming those limits and any other policies that may apply. Please confirm in writing within fifteen days of receipt of this letter.

We also request that your company preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes the claim file, photographs, vehicle data and event recordings, repair or total-loss appraisals, witness statements, recorded calls, and all communications with your insured. Any destruction or alteration of such material could seriously prejudice our client's claim, and we will pursue all available remedies should that occur.
